Good morning, Excellencies, distinguished delegates, colleagues. I declare open the 2027 sessions of the Economic and Social Council And I call to order its first meeting. Excellencies, distinguished delegates, I'm honored today to hand over the presidency of the Economic and Social Council to my predecessor. But before I give up the gavel, I hope you will permit me a few parting words. Excellencies, distinguished delegates, colleagues, and friends, it has been a privilege to serve as the President of the Economic and Social Council, one of the principal organs of the United Nations intrastate with advancing international cooperation on economic social and environmental dimensions of sustainable development, particularly at a time when the world is navigating converging crises, widening inequalities, economic uncertainty, and urgent need for renewed multilateralism. 80 years ago, the founders of the United Nations entrusted ECOSOC through Article 55 of the Charter, with advancing higher standards of living, full employment, economic and social progress, solutions to international economic and social challenges, and universal respect for human rights. Those words have stood the test of time. They remain as relevant today as they were when they were Since 1945, we have achieved much progress. We lifted millions from poverty, expanded life expectancy, and advanced human development at a pace unprecedented in human history. We expanded education and opportunity, empowering new generations to innovate, to create and to lead. We transformed global health, defeating old diseases, responding to new ones, and strengthening systems that protect the most vulnerable. We connected the world, from trade routes to digital networks, enabling ideas, goods, and people to move with unprecedented speed. We advance gender equality, amplifying the voices of women and girls and recognizing their indispensable role in shaping policies. We deepen environmental consciousness, acknowledging our shared responsibility to protect the planet and confronting the existential challenge of climate change. But again, We have challenges, challenges that test our resolve, that stretch our capacities, and that remind us that progress is never guaranteed. We confront converging crises, widening inequalities, climate pressures, financing gaps, and digital divides that risk leaving entire societies, behind. These realities demand not despair but determination. They call for a multilateral system that is more agile, that is more inclusive, and that is more accountable. That's why ECOSOC's role is important, indeed indispensable. ECOSOC has remained at the heart of the United Nations development architecture. This is the central forum where the world comes together to turn complexity into coherence, ambitions into policy, and commitments into measurable results. ECOSOC convenes diverse voices, coordinates the work of the UN systems, and catalyzes action, ensuring that our collective efforts remain focused on those furthest behind. In moments of uncertainty, ECOSOC provides directions. In moments of fragmentation, it provides unity. And in moments of crisis, it provides resolve. And it remains the bridge between global ambitions and national implementations. Excellencies, colleagues, 12 months ago, when I accepted the honour of serving as the President of the Economic and Social Council, I proposed a simple aspiration: Delivering Better. To me, those words were about strengthening confidence in multilateralism by ensuring that our work made a difference where it matters most. the most in the lives of the people. None of us could have anticipated the year that followed. Conflicts deepened, economic uncertainty intensified, development financing came under increasing strain, hard-won development gains came under growing pressure, and with only a few years left to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, The latest SDG report reminds us that only 36% of the targets are on track or making moderate progress. Amid these gaps and challenges, we were guided by the Council's vision and mandate, and by our shared commitment throughout this year. We approached every forum, every segment, every dialogue, and every negotiation with the unwavering conviction that development must remain the core principle of ECOSOC's mission and the lodestar guiding our collective efforts. Under the priorities of my presidency, we brought Member States, the UN systems, international financial institutions, multilateral development banks, academia, scientific communities, private sector, civil society, and a wide range of other stakeholders for strengthening food systems, advancing digital inclusion, supporting young people, amplifying the voices of the countries in special situations, and drawing greater attention to the growing impacts of climate change, including the risk posed by the Glaciers Lake Outpost floods. One year after the Sibiu commitment, our focus shifted from commitments to implementations. We convened the first-ever ECOSOC Special Meetings on Financial Integrity and on Credit Rating Agencies, bringing together governments, international finance institutions, investors, and private sector to help turn commitments into practical actions, because financing is never simply about finance. It is about whether countries can invest in their people, strengthen resilience, and create opportunities for future generations. Many developing countries, including my own country Nepal, are facing rising borrowing costs. Volatile energy prices, and mounting fiscal pressures, making the path towards sustainable development increasingly difficult. These pressures directly shape the choices governments can make today and the opportunities that will be available to our future generations. This year also reminded us how quickly global events reshape national realities, not least due to the continuing conflicts. For many countries, development has never been a straight path. For them, progress can take years to build, but only months and moments to set back. This is why I propose to ECOSOC Bureau the holding of a special meeting in May to discuss the economic and social effects of the ongoing disruptions of energy and supply flows, potential policy solutions, and ways in which the UN system may effectively address them. I deeply appreciate each one of you for the support you render and the contributions you made during this landmark ECOSOC meeting. Throughout this session, we also underlined the need to support countries in special situations, including LDCs, LLDCs, SEEDs, by highlighting their specific vulnerabilities, including through the joint thematic event of the General Assembly and ECOSOC on the midterm review of the Doha Programme actions for the least developed countries. We also underscored the importance of ensuring coherence, cooperation, and complementarities between the General Assembly and Economic and Social Council. The President of the General Assembly and I convened the Joint Meeting on Digital Inclusion, Innovations, and Youth Entrepreneurship. Through the Joint Meeting of the Economic and Social Council and Peacebuilding Commission, We emphasized the imperative of expanding young people's access to decent work and sustainable livelihoods, recognizing that these are the foundational pillars for both economic resilience and durable peacebuilding. We tried our best to make every segment and forum under ECOSOC more effective and impactful this year. The Bureau and myself also work to enhance the visibility of ECOSOC and strengthen awareness of its roles and contributions across the UN system and beyond. Similarly, we have excellent engagement with major groups and other stakeholders throughout this year. Dear colleagues, let me also recall that There were moments this year when agreement seemed beyond reach. Silence procedures were broken, negotiations stretched late into the night, positions appeared too far apart, and yet time and again we returned to the table, we listened, we stayed engaged even when agreement seemed out of reach. We refused to let dialogue give way to divisions. and ultimately we found common ground. The adoptions of the Financing for Development Forum outcome and the ministerial declaration of the 2026 HLPF reminded us that even in difficult times, consensus remains possible when we keep people rather than our difference at the center of our work. That experience reminded me why this Council matters. Throughout the year, I am always reminded by the wisdom in Nepal, Ekatanai Bolho, that is, unity is strength. It is a truth that has guided our nations for generations, and it is a truth that must guide our collective efforts in multilateral cooperation. When we stand together, when we listen to one another, when we respect every nation and every person, we demonstrate what multilateralism can achieve. We show that even in moments of difficulties and uncertainty, we can still find common ground in our shared interests. Excellencies, dear colleagues, earlier this year, as we commemorate the 80th anniversary of this Council, we reflected not only on its remarkable history, but on its future. Tomorrow, the General Assembly will consider the review of ECOSOC and the High-Level Political Forum. My hope is that tomorrow's deliberations will reaffirm our shared commitment to a stronger, more effective Council capable of advancing sustainable development, and restoring faith in international cooperation. The decisions we take now will shape not only the effectiveness of this Council, but the confidence that people place in multilateralism itself. At a time of mounting global challenges and deepening divides, we must ensure that ECOSOC remains a Council that listens, that convenes, and that delivers. Excellencies, colleagues, and friends, as my presidency comes to a close, I carry with me a deep sense of gratitude for the trust extended, the partnerships forged, and the shared determination to build a more just, more inclusive, and more sustainable world. I offer my sincere and heartfelt congratulations to Ambassador Omar Benjamin on his election as the next President of the Council. I wish him and the incoming Bureau every success in the year ahead. As I take pride in the achievements we have secured over the year, I am equally mindful that no precedent solves alone. On this, I thank my fellow Bureau members, Ambassadors Amr Benjamin, Ambassador Paru Onasian, Ambassadors Wellington Dario Bonscume-Castanos, and Ambassador Hector José Gómez Hernández, for your support, for your friendship, for your wise counsel, and for your constant encouragement, and engagement. My sincere appreciation also goes to the Secretariat, especially UNDESHA and DGACM, whose professionalism, quiet dedication, and tireless work made this presidency possible. Above all, I owe a special gratitude to every member state for the confidence you have placed in me throughout this year. I extend my sincere appreciation to all the co-chairs and co-facilitators of the various processes under ECOSOC, as well as the members of the Multi-Stakeholder Advisory Group to the Partnership Forum. Those include Permanent Representatives of Singapore, Germany, Austria, Zambia, Iceland, Maldives, Albania and Sierra Leone, whose stewardship, diligence, and constructive engagement have strengthened our collective work. I also wish to acknowledge former presidents of ECOSOC, whose experience, counsel, and stellar work have helped preserve the institutional strength and continuity of this Council. Their legacy reminds us that Each presidency is only one chapter in a much longer story. I thank colleagues at my Permanent Missions of Nepal. Their professionalism, tireless dedication, creativity, and unwavering commitment helped us to reach these important milestones. Excellencies, it has been one of the greatest honors of my life to serve as the President of COSAC. For Nepal, this moment stands as a defining milestone. It is the first time in the 70 years since we joined this august organization that we have had the privilege to lead one of its principal organs. Its successful conclusion is a testament to Nepal's principled and constructive diplomacy, demonstrating that Nepal can provide effective multilateral leadership, build consensus among the member states, and make meaningful contributions to shaping global policies in pursuit of our shared aspirations and common futures. Personally, this responsibility has humbled me, inspired me, and deepened my convictions in the power of multilateral cooperation. To change lives and shape a more hopeful future. Over the past year, I have had the privilege of participating in more than 250 meetings, speeches, and bilateral engagements. Each was an opportunity for me to listen, to learn, and to better understand the priorities, concerns, and aspirations of the Member States and others. Stakeholders. Those conversations have left me more convinced than ever that the Council remains one of the few places where every country, large or small, has an equal voice in shaping our common future. Even as I leave this role, the values and principles that have guided me throughout this presidency will continue to guide me beyond this presidency. It is because the world expects more multilateralism. It is because people everywhere look to the United Nations for solutions that are principled, that are inclusive, and that are effective. It is because they look to the ECOSOC for coherence, for ambitions, and for results. That touches the lives. It is because only through cooperation, through integrity and shared purpose, can we deliver better that we must. Let us be reminded of a simple yet profound truth from Nepal's wisdom, eloquently expressed in our national anthem, Swem Phulkahami Euti Mala, that is, we are hundreds of flowers weaven into one garland. It captures the very essence of multilateralism— many nations, many perspectives, diverse experiences, many journeys, yet bound together by a shared commitment to dignity, to development, and common destiny and hope. In conclusion, Excellencies, distinguished colleagues, at this cycle As this cycle concludes, I have every confidence that the best chapters of this Council are still being written. Let us make ECOSOC a beacon of hope and aspirations, driving solutions that strengthen multilateralism and deliver meaningful progress for people everywhere. To me, the Council must be The Council of Voices, where every perspective is heard. The Council of Visions, where we imagine a more sustainable and equitable future. The Council of Partnerships, where governments, communities, and stakeholders unite their strengths. And the Council of Actions, where commitments are transformed into results. And above all, the Council of Hope, where the world finds assurances, reassurances that multilateralism can still deliver for people and for the planet. This is, I believe, the ECOSOC we have worked to strengthen. This is the ECOSOC the world needs, and this is the ECOSOC that will continue to guide our collective efforts as we advance the 2030 Agenda. I thank you. May I take it that the Council wishes to elect by acclamations His Excellency Omar Benzema, Permanent Representative of Algeria to the United Nations, as the President of the Council at its 2027 session? Excellencies, dear colleagues, it is an honor and a privilege to assume the presidency of the Economic and Social Council for its 2027 session. The trust The trust and confidence placed in Algeria and in my humble person by the African Group and by all members is deeply appreciated. Steadfast commitment, under the leadership and guidance of His Excellency Abdelmajid Tebboune, President of the Republic, to multilateralism and to the promotion of international cooperation and solidarity. It is also a responsibility And I intend to carry resolutely throughout my tenure. With your support and your dedication, we will work, we will work together to accelerate the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development. Excellencies, today's world is navigating deeply interlinked challenges. Conflict persists in different parts of the world. Poverty and hunger continue to threaten millions. Inequalities are deepening. Gaps are widening. Food insecurity, debt burdens, and climate pressures continue to hinder our ability to achieve the SDGs. Against this backdrop, The 2030 Agenda remains critically off track. Only 17%— 17%— of SDG targets are progressing as intended. The financing gap for developing countries continues and is estimated at $4 trillion, $4 trillion per year. Next year, we will witness the last SDG Summit before the 2030 deadline. This is a critical juncture. We must take full use, full use of all tools at our disposal to put the SDGs back on track. This will require genuine multilateralism and also a stronger international cooperation and solidarity. It is in this spirit that the Algerian Presidency of ECOSOC has set 3 mutually reinforcing priorities for this session. First, Inclusivity. Inclusivity. Algeria will ensure that ECOSOC genuinely reflects the priorities and aspirations of all, all its members, with particular attention to countries in special situations. The Presidency will spare no efforts in creating space for all relevant stakeholders, ensuring meaningful engagement and substantive, substantive contribution to ECOSOC's works. It is equally important to give priorities to areas where further development and progress can be achieved. Second, accelerating SDGs implementations. Algeria will advocate for balanced progress across all dimensions of sustainable development, with particular focus on eradicating poverty and enhancing access to education, especially for girls, reducing inequalities, and advancing financing for sustainable development. Including, including debt relief and implementation of the Sevilla Commitment. Advancing collective environmental protection and promoting digital transformation in these areas of rapid, very rapid advances in artificial intelligence. It is equally critical to work in synergy to strengthen the role of ECOSOC in multilateral cooperation and to promote to promote more meaningful and more action-oriented deliberations. Third, reviewing trust in multilateralism and strengthening the role of ECOSOC. The Algerian Presidency aims to further reinforce trust and relevance, relevance of ECOSOC, and to contribute to strengthen its functioning. This will require encouraging the political, political engagement of all member states and all stakeholders. Contributing to the UN80 process and to reshaping the future of the United Nations. And finally, advancing resolutely the mandated review of ECOSOC subsidiary bodies scheduling. For 2027. Central to these efforts is enhancing— and I insist on that— enhancing the working method and efficiency of ECOSOC's day-to-day operations. We propose to move resolutely toward leaner, less formal interactions that prioritize substance— substance over procedural routine— by leveraging informal consultations, rationalizing the meeting calendar, and modernizing elections and decision-making procedures. Our presidency aims to save your valuable time to express your position within the Council. And to focus the Council's energy on improving implementation, implementation of its resolution and decision. Excellencies, dear colleagues, this is our vision for an ECOSOC that delivers better. But this vision will only succeed— will only succeed— with the support of each one of you. Let us work together in this last stretch before 2030. It is time for action. For concrete and robust action, it is time for implementation, accelerated and integrated implementation. It is time for result, concrete and tangible results that advance. our common agenda and leave no one, no country behind. I thank you.
